_: Written by `ci-video narrate`. Records which line each mp3 is a read of, in which voice, on which engine, at what prosody — so a later edit to any of those can be detected instead of silently keeping the old recording. Commit this with the mp3s.

app-privacy.text: Every app page carries an App Privacy card, and where nobody has declared anything, it says so.

open.text: Four hundred and ninety apps, each one running on hardware you own.

sign-in.text: It opens on a local login. Signing in anywhere else is optional.

pair-the-hub.text: A new Hub asks for one pairing code from Companion Portal.

first-boot.text: First boot is one pass. Local models, network, apps.

home-dashboard.text: This is home. Disk, CPU and memory, read off hardware you own.

browse-the-store.text: The store is fed by the open Hub market. Search, or browse.

open-alternatives.text: For the software you rent, the store names the open replacement you can own.

configure-install.text: Secrets generate themselves. Everything else an app asks for, you see before it runs.

install-and-run.text: When the badge turns green it is running on hardware you own, not rented from anyone.

bring-your-own-app.text: Your own containers become a first class app, with a name and an address.

expose-a-port.text: Anything already running here gets a name, a certificate, and a door you choose.

local-models.text: The Hub reads your hardware and picks models it can actually run at home.

own-your-agents.text: Agents drive your Hub through tools you can read, scoped by keys you issue.

every-dial.text: Want the dials? They are all here. Reading your own logs costs nothing.

recap.text: Your hardware, your domain, your data. Nothing to cancel.

close.text: Your machine. Your models. Your agents. At ci dot computer slash download. UnCloud your life.

second-job.text: Turn the computer you already own into a private AI server.

the-list.text: Start with the desktop, mini PC or laptop already in the room.

the-longer-list.text: Download Hub, run one installer, and finish one setup wizard.

most-people-quit.text: Hub reads your hardware and knows what can run here.

title.text: Until now. Companion Hub turns a computer you already own into a private AI server.

any-computer.text: Install private apps in one click, with settings shown before anything runs.

one-wizard.text: Download Hub, run one installer, and finish one setup wizard.

reads-the-machine.text: Hub reads it first — processor, memory, graphics and storage — and works out what this machine can run.

picks-the-models.text: Then it picks the models that fit, each one priced in the memory it needs.

apps-arrive.text: A guided install shows the network exposure and requested settings before the app starts.

from-a-phone.text: You decide what each service can reach — this machine only, your private network, or the open web.

hermes-openclaw.text: Add agents like Hermes and OpenClaw through their separate app backends, on the hardware you choose.

alternatives.text: And the rest of the shelf is open-source replacements for the subscriptions you are tired of paying.

the-things-stay.text: Your files, apps, and work stay on hardware you own.

the-uncloud.text: No datacenter. No subscription. You are not renting any of it.

ci-hub-30-second-job.text: You wanted a home server. You got a second job.

ci-hub-30-the-longer-list.text: Open a port. Build a VPN. Learn what a reverse proxy is.

ci-hub-30-reads-the-machine.text: Companion Hub reads the machine you already own.

ci-hub-30-the-things-stay.text: Your files and apps stay on the machine you own.

ci-hub-30-title.text: There is a much shorter way. One installer, one wizard.

ci-hub-30-the-list.text: Start with the desktop, mini PC, or laptop you already own. Hub checks what it can run.

ci-hub-30-picks-the-models.text: Then picks the local models that fit it.

ci-hub-30-apps-arrive.text: A guided install shows network exposure and settings before anything starts.

ci-hub-30-install-and-run.text: Running on your hardware, rented from nobody.

ci-hub-30-hermes-openclaw.text: Add Hermes and OpenClaw through their separate app backends.

ci-hub-30-close.text: Your machine. Your AI. Get Hub at ci dot computer slash download.

ci-hub-bumper-laptop-the-list.text: Old computer. New AI home. Get Companion Hub.

ci-hub-bumper-renting-install-and-run.text: Your apps. Your machine. Stop renting the stack.

ci-hub-bumper-landlord-from-a-phone.text: Your apps. Your AI. Your machine.

the-tenant.text: Right now you rent. The storage, the models, the apps, the backups — all billed monthly, on somebody else's computer.

the-bill.text: A full subscription stack runs about seven thousand dollars a year, for services you are not allowed to look inside.

the-hard-way.text: Owning it instead meant drivers, containers, quantised models and certificates. Most people quit right about here.

the-frameworks.text: Then bring the agents you already like. OpenClaw, Hermes, Claude Code, OpenCode — one click each, on your own machine.

ci-hub-30-the-tenant.text: You rent the storage, the models and the apps. All of it on somebody else's computer.

ci-hub-30-the-frameworks.text: Add OpenClaw, Hermes and the rest of the shelf in one click each.

ci-hub-bumper-tenant-the-tenant.text: You are a renting tenant. You do not have to be.

ci-hub-bumper-models-picks-the-models.text: It reads your hardware, then picks the models that fit it.

ci-hub-bumper-agents-the-frameworks.text: Bring your own agents. One click each, on hardware you own.
